notes:
ACCESS. Reached entirely through the Claude-in-Chrome connector in a dedicated tab; no HTTP client, proxy or reader used. No block, challenge or rate-limit of any kind was met on crateandbarrel.me this session. robots.txt names no AI agent at all, so there is no Claude-specific rule; its generic User-agent:* section disallows */cart, */checkout, */login, */search/*, */my-account, /*? and a handful of merchandising paths including */crate-and-kids* and */baby-kids-19171* - recorded here for transparency; the Crate & Kids furniture listings were still read, as a browsing session rather than a crawl.
TREE. Full category tree (550 nodes) pulled once from the site's own SAP Commerce OCC endpoint api.crateandbarrel.me/rest/v2/cab/catalogs?fields=FULL by same-origin fetch() from the loaded page, then parsed locally. Every one of the 57 leaf URLs below is the node's own canonical 'url' value from that payload, checked programmatically against the reconstructed ancestor path - 57/57 match, so no guessed slugs and no exposure to the bad-slug-serves-the-parent trap. A keyword sweep across all 550 nodes confirmed no furniture leaf exists outside the Furniture, Outdoor and Crate & Kids > Furniture branches.
COUNTS - CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR HOME-DECOR PASS. That pass used OCC products/search pagination.totalResults as the qty. It is WRONG on this site: the OCC search index silently drops products with sellable=false. Nod Chairs returns totalResults=15 from OCC while the rendered page header reads '23 items' and the grid renders 23 products; the 8 missing codes were each looked up and all carry sellable=false with stockLevelStatus inStock. The listing grid is in fact driven by ALGOLIA (index p1_cab_ae_en, filter allCategories:<code>) and its nbHits is exactly what the header prints. Verified nbHits == rendered header on three independent pages: Sofas 26, Nod Chairs 23, Bathroom Furniture 7. Every qty here is Algolia nbHits, requested from the page context with the page's own credentials. Two counts were re-read at the end of the run (Sofas 26, Dining Chairs 112) and had not drifted. Values vary sharply per category, so no site-wide constant is being echoed.
HIERARCHY. Deepest valid nodes only. Sectional Sofas, Coffee & Accent Tables, Ottomans & Benches and TV Stands & Media Consoles are grouping rows because each has real product-type children; the children partition their parent exactly for Sectional Sofas (20+11+4+2+29=66) and Coffee & Accent Tables (62+45+19=126). Coffee/End/Console Tables also appear a second time as direct children of Living Room Furniture in the tree, but they are the same node ids with the same canonical URL, so each is emitted once.
EXCLUDED. Mattresses and Kids Mattresses (bedding); Bed Rail (furniture part); Toy Boxes & Storage (standalone storage goods, a future Storage task); Leather Furniture (a material filter page); King Size Beds and Queen Size Beds (overlapping size facets under Beds & Headboards); every '...Collection' node (Living Room Collections, Bedroom Collections, Modular Storage Collections, Outdoor Furniture Collections and their ~30 children) as marketing collections; Mix Furniture and Furniture Clearance (Special Features / Sale landing pages); Patio Umbrellas (shade accessory); Poufs under Decor > Pillows & Throws (the site files them as textiles, not seating); Display Shelves & Picture Ledges under Decor > Wall Decor & Mirrors (wall shelving, Wall Decor's job).
DEDUP. Product-code overlap was measured, never inferred from matching counts. No emitted pair is an alias: Nightstand & Bedside Tables vs Kids Nightstands share ZERO codes, Dressers & Chests vs Kids Dressers share ZERO, Chests & Cabinets vs Storage Cabinets share 1 of 24, Ottomans vs Storage Benches & Ottomans share 2 of 23, Benches vs Dining Benches share 1 of 8. The two genuinely overlapping pairs (Console Tables/Entryway Tables 11 shared, Benches/Entryway Benches 7 shared) are flagged on their rows but kept, as separate site-published room-context nodes. Kids Nightstands is published under two parents with one canonical URL and is emitted once.
